meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Companies Act sector; corporate registry administered from Apia)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law principles for commercial and corporate matters, with fa'a Samoa customary law preserved in land and title matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Active: Samoa-People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1999)
Active: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus), in force for Samoa (2020), covering trade and investment framework

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Amendment Act 2019; Terrorism and Proceeds of Crime (Amendment) Act 2016; International Companies Act 1987, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018; International Companies (Beneficial Ownership Register) Regulations 2018; Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Directions (consolidated as at 2023).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO declaration, consent to act, and beneficial-ownership chain chart piercing all intermediary and nominee layers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Samoa registered agent jointly with a notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing country; if the issuing country is not a Hague Apostille Contracting State, consular legalization at the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or nearest Samoan consular officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of government-issued photo identification of each direct and indirect natural-person UBO (passport or national identity card)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or national identity authority in the UBO's country of residence; notarized by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in the same manner as the UBO declaration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address dated within 90 days (electric utility bill, bank statement, or government-issued residence registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, licensed financial institution, or municipal authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the document originates outside Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth memorandum for the founding shareholder/UBO, including due diligence on escrow and Swift wire payment sources
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank that has performed customer due diligence on the account holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the bank reference or source-of-wealth certificate is to be relied upon in Samoa

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence must screen all direct and indirect UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU sanctions lists, FATF high-risk jurisdiction statements, and Samoa's domestic terrorism and civil aviation security lists. Re-screening is required at least every 180 days and upon any ownership or payment-rail change. Because the proposed activity is ISIC 4659 surplus commercial aircraft parts distribution, the registered agent must apply dual-use/civil aviation red-flag indicators and verify the source of escrow and wire funds before any name reservation is finalized.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIFA International Companies Registry e-Services Portal (Samoa International Finance Authority, Apia)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must appear in Roman/Latin script; Samoan and English names are accepted without transliteration, while non-Latin names (including Chinese) may only be used in the private articles or constitutional documents together with a certified English translation filed at the registered agent. The registry will standardize Samoan diacritical marks and diacritics appearing in the proposed name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended for a further 30 days by filing Form IC-NAME-EXT with SIFA before the first 30-day window expires. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant or its licensed registered agent may file a written notice of administrative appeal within 14 calendar days of the written rejection. The Registrar must respond within 21 working days with written reasons; if the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Samoa by originating motion within 28 days of the dismissal. A simultaneous substitute name may be filed while the appeal is pending to avoid delaying the incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not acceptable for this entity. The International Companies Act 1987 and the Registered Agents Act 1990 require a Samoa physical address at the licensed registered agent's premises in Apia, where legal process may be served during ordinary business hours. A licensed registered agent may provide a screened shared-office arrangement for the International Company, but the agent must maintain physical files, accept service, and demonstrate substance for the medium-risk ISIC 4659 aviation spares activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated risk: estimated 25% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of active trading. The likelihood rises to roughly 40% if the registered office is shared with more than ten entities or if the aviation spares escrow flows are not adequately documented.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended (including the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2011, 2014 and 2017), ss. 4-9 (incorporation), s. 40 (registered office), ss. 44-58 (directors and officers), s. 125 (tax-exempt status); Business Licence Act 1998; International Companies Regulations 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), in administrative cooperation with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration of the Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitution) together with the prescribed Application for Incorporation (Form 1) under the International Companies Regulations 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the International Companies Act 1987 and no escrow or capital release account requirement for a Samoa International Company. The authorised share capital stated in the constitution governs issued shares; government fees and registered agent fees are payable separately.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers, having incorporated the Company under the International Companies Act 1987, do hereby: 1. ADOPT the constitution and ratify the incorporation of the International Company; 2. ACCEPT the subscription of the initial issued shares and record the allotment to the founding subscriber; 3. APPROVE the registered office at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa; 4. APPOINT the persons named in the register of directors as the first board of directors, and appoint the corporate secretary; 5. AUTHORISE the execution of the business licence application and opening of corporate bank accounts, and indemnify officers for acts taken in good faith. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; coordinated through a licensed Samoa registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request containing up to three proposed corporate names in English with the mandatory suffix Limited, Corporation, Incorporated or Ltd. The Registrar cross-checks the proposed name against the register for identical or confusingly similar names. Obtain a written non-objection before proceeding. A name implying aviation regulatory authority or government sponsorship (e.g. containing Authority, Ministry or Civil Aviation) should be avoided unless reserved for an approved entity.
required_dossiers: Brief corporate purpose statement (distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus)
Consent letter of the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit revised alternate names within five business days, or appeal the Registrar's decision to the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour under section 142 of the International Companies Act 1987, with a right to judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constituent Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent; execution before a Samoan Commissioner for Oaths or Notary Public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in the English language. The memorandum must state the company name, the objects clause covering the distribution and wholesale of certified civil aircraft rotables, avionics and surplus commercial aircraft parts (ISIC 4659), the liability limitation clause, the authorised share capital, and the appointment of the registered agent. The articles must regulate director powers, indemnification, share transfers, and the conduct of board and member meetings. Each subscriber executes the documents, and the registered agent countersigns as evidence of acceptance of the registered office appointment.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitution) in English
Certified passport copies of all subscribers
Proof of residential address of each subscriber
Consent to act as first directors and corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the constitutional documents for formal deficiency, the registered agent corrects the offending clauses and re-executes the documents; resubmission is permitted within fourteen days without loss of priority or payment of a late fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) online or counter submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend to the formal submission of Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the executed Constitution, the registered agent's consent, director and secretary consents, and evidence of payment of the incorporation fee and annual government licence fee. The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation in the prescribed statutory form, which is conclusive evidence of the company's existence and limited liability. Upon issue, the company acquires legal personality and is entitled to apply for tax-exempt status under section 125 of the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent letter of licensed registered agent
Consent to act of each director and the secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, the registered agent files a written response to the requisition within fourteen days; if rejected, the company may re-file after rectification or appeal to the Minister responsible for commerce, with reinstatement available upon payment of reinstatement fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Officers and Maintenance of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company; supervision by the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of the board or pass the pro-forma written resolution to ratify incorporation, approve the issue of subscriber shares, fix the location of the registered office, and appoint the director(s), the corporate secretary and any assistant secretary. Issue numbered share certificates and open the statutory registers, comprising the register of members, register of directors and officers, register of charges, and minute book, which must be maintained at the registered office in Samoa and made available for inspection by the Registrar upon request.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (written or meeting minutes)
Register of members with share allocation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defect in officer appointment is cured by a confirmatory board resolution or written consent signed by all directors; late filing of officer changes with the Registrar is corrected by lodgement of Form 3 and payment of the prescribed late filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Issuance of Tax-Exempt Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Samoa (formerly the Inland Revenue Department), together with the Samoa Customs Division for import-export registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Samoa Tax Identification Number (TIN) for the International Company and submit a letter requesting statutory tax exemption confirmation under section 125 of the International Companies Act 1987, which exempts qualifying international companies from Samoan income tax on offshore-sourced income. Simultaneously register the entity with the Customs Division for the future importation and re-exportation of aircraft parts and surplus materials, obtaining a customs importer-exporter code. Obtain a certificate of exemption to present to banking counterparties as evidence of the tax-neutral status of the entity.
required_dossiers: Registered agent attestation of offshore activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry for Revenue requires additional information on the offshore nature of the business, file a written clarification with the registration officer within ten business days; any formal dispute of exemption status is appealable to the Minister for Finance under the Tax Administration Act 2012.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Licence Issuance under the Business Licence Act 1998
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Licence Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), with advisory clearances from the Samoa Civil Aviation Authority and the Planning and Urban Management Agency where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standard business licence application form classifying the activity as wholesale trade in aircraft components, rotables, avionics and surplus parts. Attach the Certificate of Incorporation, the constitution, proof of lease or ownership of the registered distribution premises, the fire safety clearance, and the police clearance of the managing director. The registry assigns the licence under the Wholesale and Distributive Trade activity code as appropriate. Renew the licence annually on 1 July and display it at the principal place of business.
required_dossiers: Lease or title deed for the premises
Fire safety clearance from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority
Police clearance certificate of the principal officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business licence application is refused, the applicant may appeal to the Licence Appeal Tribunal within twenty-one days under the Business Licence Act 1998; interim operational approval may be obtained by curing the cited deficiencies such as completing the fire clearance or town planning development consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Payment Rail Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Samoa (e.g. ANZ Samoa or Bank of South Pacific) under the AML/CFT supervisory framework of the Central Bank of Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the banking package for corporate account opening, including the Certificate of Incorporation, constitution, board resolution authorising the opening of accounts and designated signatories, the business licence, tax-exempt confirmation, register of directors, and ultimate beneficial ownership declaration. Request the activation of SWIFT wire capability and the establishment of an escrow-ready settlement arrangement with the aviation escrow custodian. Complete enhanced due diligence with source-of-wealth documentation given the Medium-Risk Enhanced AML classification of the aviation spares trading model.
required_dossiers: Register of directors and beneficial ownership declaration
Passport and proof of address of all authorised signatories
Reference letter from the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a query under AML/CFT conditions, provide a supplementary source-of-funds statement and transaction flow model; if the account is declined, re-apply with a licenced Samoan bank as alternate, or apply for a letter of comfort from the Samoa International Finance Authority to confirm the entity's good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Licensing and Registration Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); advisory certification from the Samoa Civil Aviation Authority (SCAA) for the distribution of certified civil aircraft components; import-export controls administered by the Samoa Customs Division, Ministry for Revenue.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence for Wholesale and Distributive Trade in Aircraft Components, Rotables, Avionics and Surplus Commercial Aircraft Parts, together with an Approved Supplier Record under the Samoa Civil Aviation Authority if supplying parts for installation on Samoa-registered aircraft.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Preliminary Assessment) Classification B - Low Impact Trading and Storage Activity. A full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required because the operation is limited to the warehousing, inspection and wholesale distribution of certified aircraft parts with no manufacturing, electroplating, painting, chemical stripping or parts washing processes that would generate hazardous industrial effluent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge; sanitary effluent only, connected to the Samoa Water Authority municipal sewer where available, otherwise to an approved septic system meeting PUMA and Ministry of Health standards. No VOC-emitting coating or degreasing operations; where solvent-based cleaners are incidentally used, solvent VOC content must not exceed 5% w/w and operations must be conducted within closed containers to meet ambient air quality limits under the Environment Act 2003. All surplus parts, packaging, scrap metals and non-reusable materials must be segregated and removed by a licensed waste contractor under the Waste Management Regulations 2013; open burning of waste is strictly prohibited. Oil-contaminated parts and batteries must be stored on impervious bunded pallets and disposed of as hazardous waste with a manifest trail.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Evacuation and Safety Certificate issued by the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) covering the registered warehouse and office premises, including certification of fire extinguishing equipment, emergency egress and storage racking stability. Structural and land-use approval granted by the Planning and Urban Management Agency confirming the building satisfies load-bearing requirements for heavy rotables and avionics racking. Occupational safety and workplace clearance issued by the Labour and Employment Relations Division of MCIL under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013, encompassing safe manual handling procedures, racking load ratings, first aid provisions, incident reporting, and the posting of safety notices in English.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Samoa (Inland Revenue Division); official portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company is tax-exempt on offshore income and is not required to obtain an income tax ID solely by reason of incorporation. A TIN and VAGST registration number may be obtained by filing the Ministry for Revenue TIN application form with a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation or International Company licence, constitutional documents, director and shareholder identification, and a registered office certificate. The application can be lodged in person or through the registered local agent; the Ministry issues the TIN certificate and, where taxable annual turnover reaches the VAGST threshold or voluntary registration is approved, a VAGST registration certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election is available under Samoan domestic law. An International Company may elect to become a licensed international company under the International Companies Act 1987 and may voluntarily register for VAGST, payroll, or excise obligations where it transacts locally. Treaty-based hybrid mismatch rules in the Income Tax Act 2015 apply only to cross-border arrangements with treaty or structured-party exposure; otherwise entity-level exemption remains the default.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 per annum of taxable supplies; voluntary registration is permitted for businesses below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate is currently in force. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue compliant tax invoices, whether paper or electronic, showing the tax identification number, invoice serial number, date, description, amount, and VAGST charged. Electronic invoices are acceptable if retained in a format accessible to the Ministry for Revenue during audit. No API-based clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the supply of commercial aircraft parts where the goods are physically exported from Samoa and title passes to a non-resident buyer. For offshore services, zero-rating applies where the recipient is a non-resident outside Samoa and the benefit of the service is consumed outside Samoa, subject to supporting contracts and payment evidence. An International Company held under a valid international company licence remains exempt from Samoan income tax on the resulting export margin.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged through Samoa Customs Electronic Single Window
Commercial invoice issued by the International Company to the non-resident buyer
Packing list describing the surplus commercial aircraft parts and part numbers
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Samoa
Signed board resolution of the International Company authorizing the disposition of surplus inventory
Proof of payment or inward remittance certificate issued by a licensed Samoan commercial bank
ICA licence and certificate of good standing for the International Company
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may conduct deep audits of export zero-rating documentation. A false or unsupported zero-rating claim gives rise to an immediate VAGST assessment at 15%, plus a late payment penalty of up to 100% of the tax, monthly interest, and a negligence penalty of 200% of the tax evaded. Knowingly fraudulent documentation attracts criminal prosecution, fines up to WST 50,000, and imprisonment. The Commissioner has retrospective clawback authority for six years from the date of assessment, and the relevant aircraft parts may be subject to seizure at export if declaration discrepancies are detected.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Falepuna, Apia, Independent State of Samoa) - the statutory monetary authority and exchange-control administrator acting under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Exchange Control Regulations 1978, and the anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing framework supervised by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit. The Central Bank licenses authorized dealers (commercial banks), administers Samoan Tala (WST) convertibility, compiles balance-of-payments statistics, and exercises prior-approval powers over resident-entity transactions; non-resident offshore International Companies registered under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) fall outside this prior-approval perimeter when operating exclusively in foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The WST is only partially convertible. For resident entities, current-account transactions are substantially liberalized, but capital-account movements involving WST conversion or a resident counterparty (dividend remittances, loan repayments, liquidation distributions, share transfers) require Central Bank exchange-control approval. The Samoan International Company, by contrast, is a non-resident offshore person for exchange-control purposes: it may maintain and deploy unrestricted USD foreign-currency accounts, settle cross-border aircraft-part sales, remit dividends to non-resident shareholders, and repay shareholder loans without Central Bank consent and without triggering WST conversion. Profit-remittance hurdles are therefore institutional rather than regulatory: the receiving bank will require proof of economic substance, certified UBO records, current registered-agent and government licence certificates, and a documentary trail substantiating the aviation-parts trade. Once satisfied, dividends and capital distributions flow offshore freely with no exchange-control approval, no withholding tax, and no convertibility constraint. The sole capital-account boundary is the International Companies Act prohibition on conducting business with persons resident in Samoa; any such transaction would pull the affected proceeds into the resident exchange-control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1978, resident Samoan exporters must surrender the full value of export proceeds to an authorized dealer within the statutory period following export clearance (practically within 30 days), supported by declared export documentation; shortfalls and late remittances are reported by the authorized dealer to the Central Bank. This mandatory surrender and conversion regime does not apply to the WS_IC International Company. As a non-resident offshore legal person trading surplus certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics exclusively with foreign airlines, MRO providers and redistributors, the IC retains 100 percent of its USD proceeds in its offshore operating account with a zero statutory conversion ratio and no obligation to sell foreign exchange to the Central Bank or an authorized dealer. The only compliance duty is statistical: the receiving bank flags each inflow as a non-resident transactor entry in Samoa's balance-of-payments reporting. Should the IC ever derive Samoan-source receipts (a prohibited activity for an International Company), those specific proceeds would immediately become subject to the full surrender, conversion and reporting rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Offshore USD Operating Account for the International Company plus segregated Capital Escrow Account structured through the ANZ International Banking Unit
Foreign-Currency Operational Account (USD mainstream) with treasury desk support; Capital Escrow Account achievable through separately documented custody and escrow instruction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (International Company) - confirmation of registered office, registered agent, directors, secretary and members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due within 30 days after each annual anniversary of incorporation; no fixed calendar date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 200 (approx USD 74); continuing default beyond 90 days exposes the company to Registrar's notice of proposed strike-off and ultimate deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Government Renewal Fee (annual licence/renewal fee prescribed under International Companies Act 1987, Schedule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), paid through the licensed Samoa registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: remittance on or before the incorporation anniversary date each year; registered agents require cleared funds 5 business days before the due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default penalty of 10% per annum on the outstanding fee plus late filing surcharge; after six months' non-payment the Registrar may strike the company off the International Companies Register without further notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance Notification/Return (International Companies (Economic Substance) Rules 2019) - relevant for distribution and service centre activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies and Ministry of Revenue Compliance Unit, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the end of the accounting reference period (typically 31 December) or as specified in the economic substance return notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to notify may attract a penalty of up to WST 50,000 (approx USD 18,500); the Registrar may also require evidence of economic substance in Samoa and repeated defaults may trigger strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent AML/CFT Annual Client Due Diligence Refresh and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent; records must be available for inspection by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: on or before each incorporation anniversary, or within 14 days of the agent's annual customer due diligence cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-refresh may be treated as a compliance event for the licensed agent; the agent may resign, and unresolved non-cooperation leads to Registrar-initiated deregistration; corporate penalties of up to WST 200,000 apply under the AML/CFT Act 2007.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies only to a Samoa International Company that is a licensed bank, insurer, international financial services provider or trust company; commercially-licensed international companies do not require audit unless (i) directors resolve, (ii) members holding at least 10% of voting power demand one, or (iii) the Registrar orders an audit for suspected irregularities. Companies subject to the International Companies (Economic Substance) Rules 2019 must maintain auditable financial records but need not file audited accounts for the distribution activity unless directed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; US or UK GAAP may be applied for foreign-owned international companies where consistent under Samoa law. No financial statements are publicly lodged for International Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and record every transfer of shares within 14 days; the registered agent obtains a signed annual confirmation updating the shareholding and UBO schedule as at the anniversary of incorporation, and a UBO refresh notice must be completed within 14 days of any direct or indirect share transfer or change in control.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 1,600 per annum (licensed agent hosting, registered office, annual secretarial review)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 5,500 per engagement (voluntary audit or Registrar-directed audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% for a Samoa International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987, s. 205: exemption from all Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, and capital distributions for 20 years from the date of incorporation. No capital duty, no exchange control, and no deemed-profit attribution applies while the exemption remains in force.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IRC-1 Annual Income Tax Return (companies) filed through the Ministry for Revenue Electronic Services portal (MoR e-Tax). An exempt IC files a nil return and attaches its ICA s. 205 exemption certificate and a certificate of tax non-liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the year of income (standard year: 1 January to 31 December, i.e., by 31 March of the following year); a substituted accounting period requires prior written approval of the Commissioner of Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the calendar year or approved substituted accounting period and the tax identification number. Exempt ICs may quote the International Company registration number when no TIN has been issued.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned ICs file through the registered agent under a notarized power of attorney; no local TIN is required if the company relies solely on the s. 205 exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross sales and trading income, including proceeds from Escrow_Aviation and Swift wire settlement of surplus commercial aircraft parts distribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: enter 0.00; attach the ICA s. 205 exemption certificate; do not report exempt turnover as assessable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the total turnover that would otherwise be taxable but is exempt under International Companies Act 1987, s. 205 (20-year exemption).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure this line equals gross turnover and is cross-referenced to the statutory exemption; no pro-ration for non-resident ownership is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenditures (inventory cost, certification, freight, warehousing, professional fees). Exempt ICs should leave this line blank to avoid creating a taxable-loss or deduction record.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim deductions against exempt income; deduction claims may expose the IC to full assessment and records examination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions. For an exempt IC: 0.00; for a domestic-rate company: assessable income less allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: nil. If the IC derives Samoan-source domestic trading income, such income is assessable at 27% and requires a separate domestic trading licence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at 27% on Line 4, less provisional tax paid and credits. Exempt IC: 0.00.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that no withholding credits are claimed; retain final withholding certificates for any bank interest sourced in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 - Declaration and registered agent certification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed by a director or by the registered agent under the IC's registered agent engagement letter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors may sign by electronic signature; the registered agent must retain the signed authority for 7 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: immediate penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax, increasing to 10% if more than 30 days late, plus default interest of 2% per month (24% per annum). Failure to file: fine up to 200 penalty units (approx. SAT 20,000); persistent default triggers prosecution, asset attachment, and a Commissioner-issued travel ban.
